subject.title: Thinking block loop silently exhausts output tokens → session permanently unusable (976K tokens accumulated)

question: Should an exhausted provider output budget be treated as a persisted partial completion with visible recovery guidance, or should OpenClaw attempt a bounded transcript-repair/retry policy for ACP-backed sessions?
rationale: The correct behavior changes transcript durability, retry semantics, and potential side effects across heterogeneous ACP backends; source evidence does not establish a universally safe automatic recovery rule.

options.title: Define a bounded recovery contract
options.body: Require a provider/runtime-owned exhausted-output classification, surface a user-visible warning, and permit at most one side-effect-safe recovery action before preserving the session state.

options.title: Persist partial output only
options.body: Keep current persistence semantics but make exhausted output explicit to the user and provide an in-product reset or doctor recovery path.

options.title: Handle custom ACP backends externally
options.body: Document the failure as backend-specific if the captured evidence shows OpenClaw receives no reliable exhausted-output signal or safe recovery contract.

recommendation.title: Define a bounded recovery contract
recommendation.body: Require a provider/runtime-owned exhausted-output classification, surface a user-visible warning, and permit at most one side-effect-safe recovery action before preserving the session state.

likelyOwner.reason: Adjacent ACP/plugin-boundary history is the strongest available routing evidence for deciding where this cross-runtime recovery contract belongs.
